Industry observers note that upsettingly, it is that time of the week again, as Take-Two are laying off staff at Firaxis, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, only a little over a year the last time the studio suffered from layoffs. Firaxis are, notably, owned by Take-Two, the publisher of GTA 6 which comes out in, oh, two days time? Interesting timing, 'ey.

Recent findings suggest that word of the layoffs came from Bloomberg, who report that about 60 people are losing their jobs, apparently roughly a third of its staff. The studio's head, Heather Hazen, is also leaving. A spokesperson for 2K Games (the Take-Two label that manages Firaxis) shared a statement on the layoffs: "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years.

Industry observers note that "As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis." I don't feel personally confident in the idea that the only way to make a tech giant succeed is by laying a bunch of people off thereby making it much harder to make anything in the first place, especially in the lead-up to what will likely be the best selling game of the decade, but what do I know!

It has been revealed that bloomberg also report Firaxis have been working on a latest XCOM, which is yet to be revealed, but the project has apparently had to contend with numerous development issues, missing a "significant milestone over the summer." This new XCOM game hasn't been cancelled at the very least, but anonymous sources that spoke with Bloomberg stated it may have to deal with a shakeup due to the cuts. As always, solidarity with all those affected by this situation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the last couple of weeks, some Nvidia consumers noticed their SSDs were taking a hammering, reporting their driver's log file was being overwritten constantly, sometimes to the tune of 30 GB every hour. Which obviously isn't great for the lifespan of the valuable SSD you've got it installed on.

Given the problem was caused by recent driver updates, rolling back to version 621.01 was the best solution until Nvidia could do something about it. Which they did, releasing a hotfix as version 621.35. It's not available in the GeForce app yet, but you can download it directly from Nvidia's site. Not that you should.

According to recent reports, as people on the Nvidia subreddit are reporting, the problem persists. While the hotfix reduces the peak write rate and prevents it for a short while after reboot, it eventually creeps back in. One user reported that overnight the log file was still being rewritten by approximately 4.5 GB every hour.

So yeah, the best solution remains to roll back to version 621.01 and, as always with Nvidia drivers, to hold off on updating to the latest driver until it's been confirmed safe. If this ongoing saga sounds familiar, it's because the same thing happened to AMD's GPU drivers earlier this month. Maybe vibecoding driver updates and then vibecoding fixes for their inevitable bugs isn't the best way of doing things.

#121458. What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1692 w)

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1692 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, it's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto.
  • Sources indicate that it wasn't ever thus.
  • It has been revealed that during the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

Sources indicate that it wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5.

It has been revealed that during the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA. There was 2002's Manhunt, a rancid parody of snuff films – not much loved, but sufficiently admired to spawn a sequel in the hands of Rockstar London. There was 2005's adaptation of Walter Hill flick The Warriors - a mouthy Homeric beat 'em up in which you cross Latest York on foot over the course of a single night - and 2006's Rockstar Presents Table Tennis - an inexplicable pivot towards realistic sports simulation from Rockstar San Diego. Later in 2006 came Bully, aka Canis Canem Edit, a boarding school life sim from Rockstar Vancouver (née Barking Dog Studios). I didn't warm to Bully, myself, but I've never been able to get its sardonic OST out of my head.

In amongst all these, Rockstar weighed up several game projects that never made it out of the building. The aforesaid Agent is perhaps the best-known, but my conversation with Vermeij (who worked at Rockstar from 1995 to 2009) began with "Z", a fleeting attempt to expand into the world of zombie action games, which Rockstar spent a few weeks mulling over in the wake of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. It was set in the islands of Scotland, which would have made it the only Rockstar North project to unfold in the studio's backyard. "I think it was meant to be smaller than GTA, map-wise, and there weren't going to be any deserted cities - it was really just islands and some villages," Vermeij told me. "But it really didn't get that far.".

The pitch for Z couldn't be further from the sweat and glitter of GTA 6's Miami, but the two projects would have shared a taste for 'simulation' elements. "It actually was going to have cars running out of fuel," Vermeij told me. "That was going to be one of the things, and the whole idea was that you'd find cars and they'd only have a little bit of fuel in them." As for why Z never entered full development, turns out desolate North Atlantic archipelagos full of corpses can be a bit of a downer. "Everybody was super excited to do something fresh," Vermeij went on. "And then pretty swiftly, we kind of realised that it's really just a depressing version of GTA, and it sort of died.".

Sources indicate that the increasing success of Grand Theft Auto during these years was something of a "curse", Vermeij went on. It meant that a lot of Rockstar's ventures beyond GTA were eventually folded back into the series. "It's very difficult to have a studio and have one mega game, and then do something on the side," he explained. "It's almost impossible, because at any time during the development of the smaller project, management's going to say 'oh! The significant project's in trouble. We need more people.' And they're just going to pull everybody from that small team onto the big team, so even if we had progressed with [Z], what would have happened is we would have had to start GTA 4 at the same time, and eventually the small team would just be merged with the big team again.".

Recent findings suggest that rockstar's Bondalike game Agent got a lot further down the road to release than Z. It was in development for several years following GTA 4's launch, and was touted by co-founder Sam Houser as Rockstar's next megagame. "A lot of work had been done on that," Vermeij recalled. "And then we ended up just cutting and cutting it, because the same thing happened – at some point you kind of go OK, well, we better get on with the next GTA.".

In a recent development, agent sounds like it could have been a hoot, at least going by Vermeij's description of his own time with the project. It was a relatively linear, level-based action game with a touch of camp. "There was a French ski resort, and there was going to be a Mediterranean town like San Tropez, somewhere like that," Vermeij explained. "There was going to be a North African place, like Morocco or Egypt. The last level was going to be on the moon, with lasers – like Moonraker. There was another one, London or something, I can't remember. But then we just ended up cutting everything down, because what we could see happening was that at some point, we would have to go back to work on GTA. It wasn't close to being finished.".

While never a spoof in the vein of Austin Powers, Agent would have been a sillier production than the grimy and downbeat GTA 4. "It was meant to lean into all the cliches," Vermeij stated. "It was like James Bond from the 1970s - there was a girl with white boots. It wasn't a comedy, it was just completely over-the-top cliched.".

Sources indicate that as for the choice of a level-based format, this came from a desire for variety the studio couldn't realistically achieve in a GTA-style open world. "If you had to have them all on one map, you would basically have had to model a mini version of Europe," Vermeij mentioned, "So you couldn't do that." Players might have been able to revisit locations containing several missions, which calls to mind Io Interactive's later Hitman: World of Assassination games, to say nothing of their own bash at the Flemingverse, 007 First Light. "I don't how whether it was going to be completely linear, or whether you were always going to be able to visit all those locations." Vermeij said.

According to recent reports, needless to say, Rockstar's Bondalike would have featured chase scenes. Vermeij himself worked on the moving parts. "I remember doing some work on what we called the car recording stuff for GTA," he went on. "So if a level designer wanted to set up a chase scene, they would drive one car, record it, and then play back the recording, drive a second car and record that... and so driving one by one, you could set up a whole chase scene. I did a version of that for [human] characters as well, because for one of the Agent missions in the French ski resort, there was like a chase where the bad guys were on skiis and using their machine guns. So I set up a thing where you'd play them one by one, and then play the whole thing back. There was maybe like five or six bad guys and they'd ski after you, and then it was just up to the player to avoid them.".

Industry observers note that according to Vermeij, Agent never had a defined story during his time with it. It was more of a mix of scenario concepts, "kind of how we used to do games with GTA 3 and Vice City". Mind you, the absence of a nailed-down plot isn't necessarily a sign that Agent was lightyears from being finished. Even at their most byzantine, Bond movie plotlines often feel like an afterthought. "It's like oh yeah, there's a bad guy and there's a thingally-dingally that needs to be captured before the world comes to an end," summarised Vermeij. Still, Agent would spend a long time in limbo after Vermeij left. It's still unclear how much it was in active development before Rockstar's trademark finally evaporated in November 2018.

Industry observers note that one thing I learned while reading up on Rockstar's checkered history was that GTA 3, the game that made GTA a Thing on PlayStation, wasn't deemed an immediate hit at launch. According to Vermeij himself, it was months before Rockstar realised what they'd built. This inspired an obvious closing question: what might Rockstar have done, if GTA 3 hadn't blown up the way it did? Which of those other projects might have become the focus?

"I really have never thought about it," Vermeij pondered. "When Rockstar San Diego joined, it was 2002, and they already had a bunch of games and a bunch of franchises, like Midnight Club and Smuggler's Run. They were already into driving games and city games in that way, so it wouldn't have surprised me if we'd gone in that direction anyway. But then they were more about car modding and decals and stuff like that.

"At Rockstar North, we only had Manhunt and GTA," he went on. "With Manhunt, that team was in development hell for a while, they had a couple of rough years where they got stuck and in the end, they pulled through, and they got a pretty decent game. But I don't think that would have been the future. I don't think [Rockstar North] would have done a Manhunt 2. So yeah, it would be Table Tennis, I think! Everything on Table Tennis!".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that you've probably heard at least a little bit of the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack from French electronic duo, Justice: a single taken from the act's original soundtrack has been released as a standalone track, and was the accompaniment to GTA 6's launch trailer.
  • From what we've heard so far, it's all very good: synth-drenched and poppy, a perfect mix of modern electronica and nostalgic throwback - ideal for the Miami-based setting of Vice City.
  • Via a new interview with French publication Rockyrama, Justice's two members - Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay - shed a little light about their work with Rockstar, and their inspiration for joining the project.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that you've probably heard at least a little bit of the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack from French electronic duo, Justice: a single taken from the act's original soundtrack has been released as a standalone track, and was the accompaniment to GTA 6's launch trailer. Featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and the fantastic King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard, it's clear that the duo - and Rockstar - have spared no expense on the production of music for the game.

From what we've heard so far, it's all very good: synth-drenched and poppy, a perfect mix of modern electronica and nostalgic throwback - ideal for the Miami-based setting of Vice City. You ought to enjoy the music while you can, though, because it seems Justice won't be coming back to video games any time soon. If ever.

Via a new interview with French publication Rockyrama, Justice's two members - Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay - shed a little light about their work with Rockstar, and their inspiration for joining the project. "When [the offer to work with Rockstar] arrived on the table, we thought 'if there’s one video game we have to do, it's this one.' As soon as we accepted and started working [on the OST], we thought it would probably be the first and last score we’ll ever do for a video game.".

Sources indicate that interesting. The duo, from the clip we can see on Rockyrama's posts, don't seem to give more information about this decision - did they have a bad time working with Rockstar? Was it intense? Or is it rather down to the fact that, if you're going to work on a game, you may as well make it what is largely expected to be the biggest game of all time.

It has been revealed that justice, for what it's worth, consider the work they've done on GTA 6 to be "a real album" of music - it's not seen as lesser or different to the band, just because it's being released as part of a video game. "GTA 6 gave us the excuse and direction to do it. The music always had to be listenable on its own, even if each track is tailored for [a specific] scene," the band explains.

The band's album isn't the only music connected to the game, either. There's also a 34-song album launching for the game, composed of original songs from some of the biggest artists in the world. The album features Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson and many more. The full tracklist leaked at the weekend.

GTA 6 releases on Thursday, 19th November for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again.
  • To top it all off, a blog post from the devs literally refers to the alternate gender for the protag as FemJun.
  • It's been previously confirmed that no matter which gender you pick for Jun, you'll be able to romance whoever you like, so, happy smoochin'!

I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again. That's in part because the DNA of the game has been built by series vets like Drew Karpyshyn, Chad Robertson and James Ohlen. But it's also because, well, they're putting FemShep in the game. Yes, I'm being a tad facetious here, but when the latest trailer for your game is literally titled "Female Jun Reveal," well, comparisons will be made!

To top it all off, a blog post from the devs literally refers to the alternate gender for the protag as FemJun. They know what they're doing. In any case, first up, her voice actor! She's being played by Carina Conti, an up and comer last digitally heard in Mafia: The Old Country as Isabella Torrisi. Male Jun (who hasn't been given a nickname, which couldn't possibly serve to other female Jun (and MascJun is right there!)) has also had his voice actor confirmed as Stephen Oyoung, who you'll have heard as Mister Negative in Insomniac's Spider-Man games and Red Hood in Gotham Knights.

It's been previously confirmed that no matter which gender you pick for Jun, you'll be able to romance whoever you like, so, happy smoochin'! The story will stay the same too, as will dialogue options, though I'm imagine some pronoun switcheroos will take place somewhere along the line.

Industry observers note that I'm mostly just left feeling that this doesn't really seem like it'll fix the game's boring hero problem. Edwin made note of Jun's quite lacklustre vibe earlier this year, aptly tearing down MascJun's Instagram visage, though this was prior to the face model and voice actor change the character has undergone. Personally, I'm not sure that'll be enough, and FemJun kind of matches that Instagram look; the perfect bun and bangs that pop out when she takes her helmet off is quite silly too. Ah well! A game isn't done until it's done (which, in theory, will be April 7th next year).

Early on in GTA 6, you'll gain access to the JoySystem, a game console with a handful of games you can play. One of those is Tenebrae Lux, a black and white, first-person puzzle game. In this GTA 6 guide, we have a Tenebrae Lux walkthrough, guiding you through the puzzles to reach the ending.

Tenebrae Lux features randomised elements in some of its puzzles, so your experience may vary from what you see in our images and videos.

Below is our walkthrough of Tenebrae Lux, revealing puzzle solutions and where to find notes.

There are 11 notes to collect in total, but the last two require you to collect the previous nine.

In a single playthrough of Tenebrae Lux, you can find those 9 notes hidden in 17 possible locations. Collecting these 9 notes will then allow you to find the 10th and 11th notes.

After waking up on the island, you must solve at least three grid-based puzzles located on the beach, though there are five to find in total — two of which are necessary if you're looking for every note.

Awaken on the beach and make your way to the shelter on the horizon, as pictured:.

Go inside the shelter and head for the wooden boxes directly opposite the entrance:.

On the table you'll find Note Location #1, as pictured:.

Industry observers note that immediately next to Note Location #1 is a board you can interact with. This is Board Puzzle #1.

As is the case with all the other Board Puzzles, Board Puzzle #1 is randomly selected from a batch of puzzles; you won't always be presented with the same one.

To solve the puzzle, follow the steps in the below videos depending on which puzzle you have in front of you:.

In the same area as Board Puzzle #1, you'll find Board Puzzle #2 just to the right of the entrance as you enter. For context, the location is pictured:.

After checking Note Location #2, go inside the shack:.

On the right-hand side are some hooks; this is Note Location #3, where you may find a note hanging with some rope and a set of scales:.

Industry observers note that after checking Note Location #2, enter the shelter to the right. This is what it looks like:.

Go inside through the front entrance, as shown:.

Head towards the wooden crate at the back-right part of the building:.

Here are the possible solutions we've found so far:.

After solving Board Puzzle #3, turn around and leave the shack through the door ahead:.

Turn right and inspect the railing; this is Note Location #4, where you may find a note on the railing:.

After checking Note Location #4, go around to the front of the shack, where you entered the first time:.

To the right of the entrance are a couple of crates; this is Note Location #5, where you may find a note resting against the crates:.

After solving Board Puzzle #3, exit the shelter and go left along the coast (it's quite a walk):.

You will pass a small dock with a door on it to your left, ignore it and continue forward:.

Head for the light in the distance:.

Here you'll find Board Puzzle #4 next to a shipping container:.

Here are the possible solutions we've found so far:.

In a recent development, the goal is to input the correct string of numbers into the telephone on the back wall. However, there is no defined phone number for you to use; it is a randomised solution.

To learn the phone number, you must pass through several incarnations of the same room to discover differences in the environment, one by one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the most sought-after products in Black Friday sales are Apple's iPads. These powerful tablets often cost a lot, and rarely see discounts, so a reduction in price becomes all the more tempting. But if you're just looking at the recent models, you're missing a trick.

Walmart is a major seller of restored iPads, or second-hand slates that have been professionally returned to a near-new condition. Tablets like this are often much cheaper than new ones, and work just as well (you can take my word for it, I bought a refurbished 2020 iPad Pro and it still works perfectly). While these models are cheaper anyway, Walmart is offering Black Friday deals on a fair few of them, bringing tablets down to remarkably cheap prices. These are mostly for older models, with a 2021 release the newest here, but they're still powerful and modern slates and so you might find an older iPad suits you fine.

Perhaps the best refurbished iPad deal is this: over a third off the price of a large-screen iPad. It's the 2020 model, but I can promise it still works fantastically since that's the one I own (and bought refurbed). I wish I could've found it at this price.

If you want a smaller iPad, this is the best deal for you; it's the only serious discount on an iPad mini, and 40% off is great. It's only the 64GB model, but one with cellular connection, so you can easily use cloud storage instead.

This is a much older iPad Pro, so you're buying this discount for the large screen rather than modern specs. It has more storage than many other of these refurbished models, at 128GB.

According to recent reports, another modern-build tablet in Walmart's refurb sales is this 2020 iPad Air, and its discount brings it to the lowest price of any home button-less model on this list. It's for the smaller 64GB model.

This is an older iPad, but it still works well (even without being restored), and so $140 is a really good price for it. The extra bargain is in the accessories you're getting with it: a protective case and charging cable are both included with the tablet.

If you've been looking for a newly introduced slate, changing tack in the Black Friday iPad deals to buy an older, refurbished model might seem might seem unthinkable.

In a recent development, older slates work just well for tasks like word processing, streaming video, communications and simple workflow tasks. Slack has never challenged my 6-year-old iPad Pro. The trappings of newer slates, like advanced chipsets, will only really pay off for intensive tasks like video editing.

It has been revealed that what about gaming? From my experience, older tablets still run the most advanced games pretty well. After all, game makers don't want to limit their potential audience by excluding owners of older tech, so they optimize their games to work well on various devices.

The only problem with older tablets is that they are less battery-efficient, even in refurbished models which usually enjoy newly introduced batteries. Basically any game more complex than NYT Games will sap battery quite promptly, so I only game on my iPad when I'm at home and near a power supply.

So if you're weighing up between an old or latest slate, where you plan to play is the big thing worth considering.

If you're considering rivals, we've also got a round-up of the best gaming tablets, so you can see how iPads stack up against Android counterparts.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Disneyland live entertainment is few and far between as of late, which is a shame considering the Anaheim theme park used to boast some of the best reveals.
  • Sources indicate that the fire reportedly broke out during Fantasmic’s second performance of the night shortly before the show’s finale.
  • Recent findings suggest that here’s the Mark Twain Riverboat running during Fantasmic last night with the fire behind it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disneyland live entertainment is few and far between as of late, which is a shame considering the Anaheim theme park used to boast some of the best reveals. On November 21st, one of the last and most beloved nighttime shows, Fantasmic, went up in flames for the second time in three short years. With two incidents and Disney’s desire to cut back on live entertainment, I’m really starting to worry about the future of the show.

Sources indicate that the fire reportedly broke out during Fantasmic’s second performance of the night shortly before the show’s finale. While the Mark Twain finale was able to go on, flames can be seen behind the boat on the small stage set up on Tom Saywer Island. Guests at the park were quick to pull out their phones and film the growing flames as the Mark Twain, full of classic Disney characters, made its way around the river. Take a look:.

Recent findings suggest that here’s the Mark Twain Riverboat running during Fantasmic last night with the fire behind it. This happened during the 10:30PM show https://t.co/bMcOZ6z0PtNovember 22, 2026.

The last two minutes of the show were canceled, and guests were asked to vacate the viewing area while the fire department handled the blaze. Thankfully, the fire was small compared to the 2023 incident that turned the Maleficent dragon animatronic into a giant fireball and forever changed the show. There’s been no word on the extent of the damage this time around, but considering the show was back Sunday night it safe to assume that nothing was affected and no cast members were harmed, thankfully.

In a recent development, two fiery incidents are definitely a cause for concern, and with Disneyland executives’ history of scaling back entertainment to cut costs, I can’t help but worry about the show’s fate. After all, Fantasmic boasts a large cast of incredible performers and several floating units. Plus water screens, projectors, and fireworks. I’m no expert, but I’m willing to bet it’s one of the most costly attractions at Disneyland. Not to mention, the show is still feeling the loss of the Maleficent Dragon, which makes the battle between Mickey and Maleficent lackluster.

In a recent development, while I don’t think Disneyland would end the show without also announcing a replacement, I do think Disney fans should prepare themselves. After all, Disney fans aren’t known for taking fresh changes well. Just look at the uproar that happened when it was announced Dinosaur would close to make room for a new Indiana Jones attraction at Disney World.

Disneyland has been having a rough go at things this month. On the first day of the holiday season, the Anaheim theme park’s iconic fake snow was accidentally turned on during a rainstorm, creating a mess. Back in October, Frontierland experienced widespread flooding. With park tickets being so expensive, it’s unfortunate to see cracks in Disneyland’s magic, but not even the mouse can control the weather or unexpected fires.

Everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

It has been revealed that the world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

Every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

#121449. Latest Update: "Encouraging players to return is no mean feat" - Square Enix tempts Final Fantasy 14 players back with free game-time to fill void before upcoming expansion

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (561 w)

Latest Update: "Encouraging players to return is no mean feat" - Square Enix tempts Final Fantasy 14 players back with free game-time to fill void before upcoming expansion

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (561 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, final Fantasy 14 is between expansions at the moment, with Evercold preparing for release in February.
  • This promotion, which began yesterday, offers players a choice between two enticing freebies.
  • In addition, there's an alluring character skip available too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, final Fantasy 14 is between expansions at the moment, with Evercold preparing for release in February. So, in order to keep the game populated for the next few months, Square Enix is running a special promotion in hopes of tempting players back in.

This promotion, which began yesterday, offers players a choice between two enticing freebies. Lapsed players who haven't logged in for over six months are to be given 30 days of free game time to hop back in and catch up with the main story quest ahead of Evercold's release.

In addition, there's an alluring character skip available too. If your FF14 character is at least level 90 on one class - the current level-cap is 100 - you can skip all the way to the final part of the latest Dawntrail expansion. You still need to grind to level 100 in preparation for Evercold, but the aforementioned free month of game time should provide plenty of time to do so.

In a producer letter written to accompany this promotion, Naoki Yoshida provided insight into why this was being implemented, stating that retaining players in an MMO like FF14 was of the "utmost importance".

"Encouraging players to return is no mean feat", Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually upgrade the game to address such issues, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed.

Sources indicate that "For one, I feel that the pace of change in our lives is growing increasingly fast. Back when A Realm Reborn rolled out, I set policies in place based on the idea that significant changes in life usually happened in roughly three-year cycles. With that in mind, we've done our best to avoid heavy-handed attempts to secure player retention through game design, and we still maintain that philosophy even today.".

Yoshida went on to explain that promotions such as this are meant as a "tiny nudge". He notes that those who have retained subscriptions continuously remain "the most vital" players in the development team's eyes, and acknowledges that the process of catching up in an MMO can seem "daunting" for many.

In a recent development, this problem of player retention is nothing new for MMOs, especially in the tricky time between the end of a current expansion and the beginning of a new one. MMO popularity often waxes and wanes, with a new expansion acting as an exciting call to action, with the months leading up to it often serving as a natural break-point for many. Still, monthly subs pay the bills, so keeping folks around even during these quiet months is key.

Final Fantasy 14: Evercold is looking like an especially exciting expansion. On top of the upcoming story and two classes being added, the game is getting an overhaul to combat, with both classic Reborn and Evolved action modes, as well as a new raid difficulty meant to bridge the gap between normal and savage tiers.

The game has certainly come a long way since its initial release back in 2010. Dawntrail proved divisive among fans too, though with Evercold there's a lot of hope that a new overarching storyline can bring the steal back the hearts of players old and new.

SNEG has re-released three more venerable PC strategy games including Warlords 4: Heroes of Etheria

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that as well as giving a spit-and-polish digital release to various Warhammer classics, antique D&D games, and the cult ellipsoid horror games in the Ecstatica series, SNEG has been bug-fixing a bunch of strategy games from years gone by and getting them up on Steam and GOG.
  • Industry observers note that warlords 4 was the final turn-based game in the beloved series, with the RTS spin-off series Warlords Battlecry already two games deep by the time of its release in 2003.
  • Soldiers at War took the X-COM/UFO turn-based tactics formula—this was 1998, X-COM still had a hyphen—and applied it to World War II.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that as well as giving a spit-and-polish digital release to various Warhammer classics, antique D&D games, and the cult ellipsoid horror games in the Ecstatica series, SNEG has been bug-fixing a bunch of strategy games from years gone by and getting them up on Steam and GOG. The latest trio to appear on digital platforms are Theocracy, Soldiers at War, and Warlords 4: Heroes of Etheria.

Industry observers note that warlords 4 was the final turn-based game in the beloved series, with the RTS spin-off series Warlords Battlecry already two games deep by the time of its release in 2003. This updated version supports resolutions up to 4K, and incorporates community fixes and a community-made campaign. It's available on Steam and GOG.

Soldiers at War took the X-COM/UFO turn-based tactics formula—this was 1998, X-COM still had a hyphen—and applied it to World War II. You'd choose a squad of eight from your platoon of 32 each mission, fighting through a campaign that started in North Africa and ended in Germany, gaining experience along the way. SNEG's version supports 1280x720 widescreen resolution. It's available on Steam and GOG.

Theocracy narrowly beat Total War to the punch in March of 2000 with its mix of turn-based civilization management and real-time battles, tasking you with uniting Aztec tribes before the prophesied Spanish invasion. You're on the clock with 100 years to use diplomacy, trade, and warfare to bring together an empire that can stand the test of time. The updated version still has a resolution of 800x600, but uses FSR 1 to scale up for modern displays. You'll be shocked to learn, it's also available on Steam and GOG.

Recent findings suggest that all three games are designed to be easy to run on modern Windows systems, and have cloud saves and achievements. I'm tempted by Warlords 4, which I didn't play at the time because I'd moved over to the real-time Battlecry games by then. But I've still got fond memories of Warlords 2 Deluxe, which had 60 different worlds so if you were tired of raising griffon armies in its generic fantasy land you could conquer something oddball like Dante's Inferno instead. Or even make your own, right down to pixel-crafting the unit art. Good times.

Is it time to retire Dragon Quest as a series? Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it might be

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (426 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it may be time for Square Enix to retire Dragon Quest, while reflecting on the direction of the popular RPG series after Akira Toriyama's death.
  • Today, speaking via a blog post on his personal website (hat tip, Power Up Gaming), Mitsuda - a colleague of Toriyama's back in the SNES/Chrono Trigger days - suggested that maybe it's time to retire the franchise in favour of something new.
  • "The Toriyama-style illustrations for [Dragon Quest RPG] have become a hot topic, but I feel that this direction is not good for the artist, Toriyama Akira fans, and even for the late Toriyama Akira himself," stated Mitsuda.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it may be time for Square Enix to retire Dragon Quest, while reflecting on the direction of the popular RPG series after Akira Toriyama's death. The mangaka, whose art and distinct style were foundational to Chrono Trigger and Chrono Cross - and are still used in Dragon Quest to this day - died in 2024 at the age of 68.

Today, speaking via a blog post on his personal website (hat tip, Power Up Gaming), Mitsuda - a colleague of Toriyama's back in the SNES/Chrono Trigger days - suggested that maybe it's time to retire the franchise in favour of something new. This was all triggered by the announcement of Dragon Quest RPG: The Island of the Demon Tree and the Guided Island, an iOS and Android game that uses art that is very reminiscent of Toriyama's.

"The Toriyama-style illustrations for [Dragon Quest RPG] have become a hot topic, but I feel that this direction is not good for the artist, Toriyama Akira fans, and even for the late Toriyama Akira himself," stated Mitsuda. "As a personal opinion, since it's impossible to create anything truly new no matter how hard you try, I feel that the Dragon Quest series should be brought to an end for now, and [Dragon Quest creator, Yuji Horii] should create a new RPG. (There have been many remakes already.)".

Horii himself seems undeterred: with the new mobile game's announcement last week, he noted that the goal of his new project is to "capture that unmistakable Dragon Quest feeling" that comes with "exploring towns, meeting new allies, gearing up and steadily growing stronger". As Mitsuda calls for the series to retire, and for something new to take its place, Horii is keen to bring "the same classic adventure" to your smartphone.

According to recent reports, "What's key is that the game provides dreams, hope, and experiences that can only be had through games to the younger generation of children who will play it in the future," concluded Mitsuda. "But every time I see topics like this, I realise just how wonderful Dragon Quest is and how it has captivated so many people.".

It's unlikely Square Enix is going to want to drop the series, of course: the Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake exceeded Square Enix's (in)famously lofty expectations, and as the organization aggressively pursues its multiplatform strategy, it's hard to imagine a world in which it's going to want to move away from a series that routinely pulls in millions of sales.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.

It has been revealed that "What if you could create your own Dead by Daylight experiences?" explains a blog post recapping the intends for how the game is going to change. "As one of the most exciting updates coming in 2027, the Dead by Daylight Workshop will open the doors to user-created content in some incredible ways. From designing your own Maps and importing custom assets, to modifying game rules, objectives, and even creating entirely upcoming modes, the possibilities are vast.".

Industry observers note that the post goes on to note that anything created in the workshop will "exist separately from all our classic modes, with dedicated creation tools and moderation provided to ensure experienced modders have everything they need to do their best work, and all submissions meet our official guidelines." I am always hesitant when it comes to UGC faff, because the ability to make your own custom Debbie Daylight maps might sound promising, but people do actually have to engage with them for the whole thing to work. It's just putting a hat on a hat!

Anyway, the workshop isn't the only thing Behaviour have in the works. For one, the game is getting a substantial visual overhaul. You can expect lighting improvements, more detailed assets and "tons of atmospheric touches," alongside revamps of particular maps like the Temple of Purgation and Backwater Swamp. Killers and survivors will be getting some TLC too by "improving character textures, proportions, hair, and animations to make them look and feel more lifelike. That includes updated character rigs, new motion capture, and new facial animation technology designed to better express a character’s fear, pain, and struggles over the course of a Trial.".

Beyond all of that, a dynamic weather system is coming to the game, meaning you'll now have to deal with the likes of rain, thunderstorms, snow and heavy wind, all of which can impact matches. Onboarding for newer folks should be getting some improvements too, with the addition of a "more cinematic introduction, clearer explanations and tutorials of game mechanics, and a more gradual introduction," to the game. All of this will be coming in one significant patch sometime in 2027, so, keep your eyes peeled for whenever that drops.

Sony has shared a selection of staggering statistics relating to the launch of GTA 6 on PS5.

From launch on 19th November through to the end of the title's opening weekend, Sony recorded over 39 million unique players.

The game set a new record on PlayStation for the highest number of concurrent players on any game.

PS5 players have logged 683 million hours of GTA 6 playtime, and on average, every owner on PlayStation has played it for 17.4 hours.

According to recent reports, outside of the console's launch and Christmas holidays, the launch of GTA 6 resulted in "the largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day". GTA 6 was the first game played on 70% of those new PS5 systems.

Sources indicate that the day after release, Rockstar Games announced GTA 6 had sold 32.5 million units across PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. With these fresh stats from PlayStation, we know it's sold over 39 million copies on PS5 alone, as of yesterday.

GTA 6 will continue to sell for years to come, as there'll be a PC version next year along with a brand latest iteration of GTA Online. We've got a 10/10-rated GTA 6 PS5 review on the site, and we're working on our comprehensive GTA 6 guide right now.

For six seasons now, Abbott Elementary fans have faithfully watched the relationship between Janine Teagues (Quinta Brunson) and Gregory Eddie (Tyler James Williams) progress. The pair have gone from good friends to committed lovers over the past several years and, now, it seems we’re on the cusp of a proposal. Many viewers are hoping an engagement will come during the Disneyland-set 100th episode that’ll air amid the 2026 TV schedule. I’d love that as well, but I also have a question about two other characters.

According to recent reports, gregory and Janine are, of course, the core couple on Abbott, but plenty of other romantic relationships amongst characters have been highlighted as well. As we anticipate what lies ahead for Janine and Gregory, I can’t help but wonder what the future holds for Ava Coleman and O’Shon, who’ve been dating since Season 4. I’ve enjoyed seeing their relationship develop as well as the funny moments that have resulted from that. With that, it’s hard not to wonder what the long-term plan for them might look like.

Recent findings suggest that it’s clear that the affable O’Shon (Matthew Law) and Abbott’s diva of a principal Ava (Critics Choice winner Janelle James) are on steady footing after some initial growing pains. At this point, the pair have not only vacationed together, but they’ve also reached the point where they can throw a party as a couple. (That Halloween shindig they held this season was fantastic). Some may think it’s a bit early to consider a proposal for these two, but I don’t think it’s wild to think it could happen by the end of Season 6.

Industry observers note that gregory first expressed interest in proposing to Janine at the end of Season 5, which was about two years after the two finally got together. Ava and O’Shon will be reaching that mark later in the sixth season and, while great TV couples have different timelines, I could see O’Shon popping the question soon. Plus, given how encouraging O’Shon has been amid Gregory’s attempts to propose, who’s to say the former doesn’t want that for himself sometime in the near future?

Of course, I’m not saying anyone needs to be jumping the broom by the end of this season. I just wouldn’t mind seeing one or two engagements by the time Abbott’s finale rolls around next spring. That may seem like a long shot for Ava and O’Shon right now, but I’m feeling very good about Janine and Gregory’s chances of hitting that milestone.

The True Story That Inspired Abbott Elementary’s Choice To Move The School Into A Mall.

Gregory has been trying to orchestrate the right moment to present Janine with a ring. During the show’s latest episode, “Competition,” he attempted to land a reservation at a popular Italian restaurant, where he could propose. Ironically, that strategy became moot once Abbott’s Step Team punched their ticket to Disneyland, and Janine informed her man that they’d serve as chaperones on the trip. So it now seems like a given that Gregory will attempt to propose while he and his lady are in “The Happiest Place On Earth.”.

It has been revealed that what’s more is that the pressure is going to be on, as Janine is aware of her beau’s intention to pop the question (thanks to a major slip-up on Ava’s part). So the pressure is really on for Eddie to craft the perfect proposal. The Disneyland episode could indeed present him the right situation to do just that and, if Gregory does pull it off in great fashion, it might set a bit of a bar for O’Shon to clear if he eventually takes that step.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, your workstation is separated into sections, and you’ll need to tab between them to complete your order swiftly and accurately.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I have a real soft spot for games that simulate cooking. A strange thing given my aversion to crafting mechanics, but cooking? I could do that all day.

It has been revealed that kuloNiku: Bowl Up! Is right up my alley, then. Developed by Gamebir Studio, it sees you take on the role of a fresh meatball restaurant owner. Your job is to pay close attention to your customers’ orders to ensure maximum satisfaction, thus increasing your reputation and revenue.

According to recent reports, your workstation is separated into sections, and you’ll need to tab between them to complete your order swiftly and accurately. Someone orders a Classic Bowl with extra chilli? You’ll need to grab your bowl, go straight to the cooking pan, add three meatballs and one noodle nest, then tab over to the chopping board, grab your chilli and finely slice it. Once that’s added, tab back to your pan, chuck the meatballs and noodles into your bowl, add a ladle of broth, then go to your seasoning station. Add a blob of sweet soy sauce and your cutlery, then serve.

Industry observers note that if you nail your customer’s order, they’ll shower you with praise and chuck a few coins into your tip jar. Get something wrong and they’ll let you know, but there generally isn’t any major penalty. If you really mess up, your customer may ask for a full refund, lowering your reputation.

As you complete orders and memorise your recipes, you’ll complete tasks a lot faster. It’s such a tactile experience, too. Using an on-screen cursor, you have to manually select each ingredient while having direct control over your knife when slicing through veg. It serves as the perfect game for mouse controls on Switch 2, giving accuracy that feels otherwise limited via analogue controls. In handheld, the touchscreen can be used to cycle through dialogue but not for cooking.

In addition to cooking, you can decorate your restaurant, visit the shop to purchase upcoming ingredients and items, and nurture your relationships with NPCs during your time off. This usually involves visiting new areas of the neighbourhood and engaging in dialogue. Each area is a static background, so don’t go expecting to wander around; the focus will remain on your conversations.

Sources indicate that finally, you have Meatball Brawls, or ‘Meatbrawls’. These are scheduled competitions in which you showcase your cooking skills to be judged against an opponent. You’ll need to be on your toes with this, as the judges and audience throw in fresh requests in the heat of battle, forcing you to reconsider your flow to accommodate upcoming ingredients. Win the brawl, and you’ll gain an even stronger reputation.

Overall, I found all of the activities outside of the kitchen to be fun enough, but I was constantly eager to get back to cooking. If the game is missing a key ingredient, it’s a mode in which you just cook recipes over and over. The main campaign limits you to just three customers per in-game day, which is a shame. Otherwise, it’s a great time for budding restaurateurs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mario Kart World just got a massive new upgrade in version 1.9.0, finally bringing Nintendo's Switch 2 racing game into the limelight – but not all fans are satisfied.

Nintendo unveils 1.9.0 in a colorful trailer on YouTube, featuring eight "new" tracks and two Knockout Tour routes – and yes, the quote marks around the word "new" are intentional on my part. That's because the tracks are sequels of sorts, acting as the "two" counterparts to already existing maps: Airship Fortress 2, Desert Hills 2, DK Pass 2, Maio Bros. Circuit 2, Koopa Troopa Beach 2, Salty Salty Speedway 2, and Wario Stadium 2.

In a recent development, fans are jokingly calling 1.9.0 the "enhancement of 2s" in the comments, noting that there isn't one truly latest map in the lineup here. They're just reverse takes on old tracks, really. "This update certainly has 'The Power of Two' in it," reads one reply. Another jests, "This is like if McDonald's slapped a McChicken inside a McDouble, put it in a new box, and called it a brand-new menu item," clarifying they're "not mad at this update, though.".

There is still 2.0 to look forward to, after all – and players note that's likely why Nintendo hasn't dropped anything too significant in 1.9.0. "People don't seem to realize we're getting close to a 2.0 patch," as one response puts it. "That's the big one that will have a lot of stuff that probably people are looking for and stuff that people aren't expecting." As for the Knockout Tour routes, this week's patch also brings two: Feather Rally and Lucky Cat Rally.

In a recent development, the fresh version includes plenty of other changes, as outlined on Nintendo's official support website. They range from technical to wholesome, like the fact that "confetti now falls during the results presentation in Grand Prix and Knockout Tour." Folks can also now pass through the river route to Cheep Cheep Falls from DK Pass, Sky-High Sundae, Salty Salty Speedway, Starview Peak, and Wario Shipyard.

All in all, it's not a bad update – heck, at least it's something seeing the love Nintendo's given Mario Kart 8 recently – but it does leave ample room for a banger 2.0, if you ask me.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

DOOM: The Dark Ages was originally designed as an Xbox exclusive, but late decisions led it to being ported to PS5.

The news comes from a Kiwi Talkz podcast, where host Reece Reilly was joined by three former id Software devs to discuss all things DOOM, Xbox Game Pass, id Software work culture, layoffs, and more.

Interestingly, quite far into the conversation, ex-id software employee Jordan Turner claims that "originally [DOOM: The Dark Ages] was going to be Xbox exclusive" up until "fairly late in the process".

"And in Dark Ages' case too, originally the game was going to be Xbox exclusive, and then fairly late in the process, we were porting to PS5. And at that point, we were still like, is our goal premium sales? In certain studio meetings, Marty [Stratton] would say stuff like, when we got it on Battle.net - 'it's another premium platform to put the game on'".

It has been revealed that reacting to Turner, Reilly goes on to critic the Xbox Game Pass model, saying he doesn't "understand it" and that it "devalues games". The conversation continues with a discussion about a lack of clarity and protection from Microsoft when developing games for Xbox Game Pass, and how id Software exec Marty Stratton felt porting to PS5 was "another premium platform to put The Dark Ages on" (as seen above).

It has been revealed that speaking to IGN in 2024, former Xbox CEO Phil Spencer described DOOM as a franchise that "everyone deserves to play", recalling a meeting between Stratton and himself in which the id Software exec said "he wanted to sell it on all platforms. Simple as that".

Back in July, the DOOM developer was dealt a massive blow as part of Xbox's planned 'Reset', which saw id Software lay off a significant portion of its team.

id Software still remains an Xbox first-party developer, and is "already working on its next game", according to Xbox boss Asha Sharma's recent post on social media.

Would you have liked to have seen DOOM: The Dark Ages as an Xbox exclusive? Let us know in the comments below.

[source youtube.com, via ign.com].

  • As much as Call of Duty is criticised for delivering the same thing every year, reports occasionally surface of attempts to take the series in bold upcoming directions, even if none of these experiments have so far seen the light of day.
  • Industry observers note that this latest revelation comes from Infinity Ward veteran Taylor Kurosaki, who led development on the studio's Infinite Warfare and 2019 Modern Warfare game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As much as Call of Duty is criticised for delivering the same thing every year, reports occasionally surface of attempts to take the series in bold upcoming directions, even if none of these experiments have so far seen the light of day. And it turns out a medieval Call of Duty was also explored at one time.

Industry observers note that this latest revelation comes from Infinity Ward veteran Taylor Kurosaki, who led development on the studio's Infinite Warfare and 2019 Modern Warfare game. "Call of Duty is a massive tree with a lot of branches, right?" Kurosaki told PC Gamer. "It can be World War 2. The team at IW had prototyped a medieval Call of Duty. Where you were a knight and had a sword and all kinds of crazy shit. But if it's a war story, sure, it can be Call of Duty.".

In a recent development, this isn't the first time we've heard of an unusual Call of Duty prototype. When Activision brought Sledgehammer Games into the fold as another lead studio for the lucrative shooter series, the team briefly worked on a third-person horror off-shoot set in Vietnam, which was referred to as Fog of War.

Activision's legal battle with Infinity Ward founders Vince Zampella and Jason West, however, caused the project to be cancelled, as Sledgehammer was roped into helping the studio finish Modern Warfare 3.

According to recent reports, as for Kurosaki, he currently leads That's No Moon alongside creative partner Jacob Minkoff and other Infinity Ward and Naughty Dog veterans. The studio is currently working on Crossfire, a narrative-driven third-person shooter set in the universe of Smilegate's free-to-play series of the same name.

Recent findings suggest that I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

The stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

Recent findings suggest that it's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

Industry observers note that getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

In a recent development, while most videogames got out of the way of Grand Theft Auto 6, on the day of its release The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth's free online DLC Repentance+ released an update. It included an easter egg daily challenge called Crime Mode (the seed is V1CE BSMT) with references to GTA like a wanted rating, guns, cops, and cars. Well, driveable minecarts.

Sources indicate that what should have been an easy PR win for publisher Nicalis quickly turned sour as players pointed out that the music in Crime Mode sure sounds AI-generated. "It has that 'tinniness' that something like Suno generated music has", user ShweetStuff noted before looking at the music files and finding that, yep, there was Suno metadata in the file comments. Yet there was no AI disclosure on the DLC's Steam page.

Players were not thrilled by this development. Steam user reviews on The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ dropped to Overwhelmingly Negative, with only 8% positive recent reviews. Players put the blame on Nicalis, who licence Binding of Isaac from its original creator Edmund McMillen. "Edmund please take back control of the game", one mentioned.

"Woke up to a shit show," McMillen wrote on the hatesite formerly known as Twitter when he found out what had happened, "obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned.".

Industry observers note that as of the latest enhancement, the AI-generated music is gone. "It's a little sad given Joey Kuras (game's sound designer) did some excellent sounds for Mewgenics", ShweetStuff wrote, "but I suppose this is the industry nowadays!".

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is the US' best-selling physical game so far this year

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (295 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The very popular and critically-acclaimed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has set another record.
  • The remake has sold more than 1m physical copies in the US alone in its launch week (ending 7th November).
  • In a recent development, while Nintendo games tend to perform better at retail than those from Sony, Xbox or third-party publishers, physical sales in general have been declining in the US.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The very popular and critically-acclaimed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has set another record. After selling 5.2m copies in four days and becoming the Switch 2's fastest-selling game, Ocarina of Time has now been revealed to also be a major seller at retail.

The remake has sold more than 1m physical copies in the US alone in its launch week (ending 7th November). That's according to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella, who revealed on Bluesky that the record also makes it the first title to surpass 1m physical sales since 2023's Tears of the Kingdom. That is, no other game - from any publisher - has managed to sell over 1m copies in the US within its first week in three years.

In a recent development, while Nintendo games tend to perform better at retail than those from Sony, Xbox or third-party publishers, physical sales in general have been declining in the US. In July, Piscatella revealed that just seven PlayStation games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies up to that point in 2026, and that was after all the backlash to Sony's decision to end physical disc manufacturing by January 2028.

In a recent development, ocarina of Time's lead of this particular segment likely won't continue, however. That's because, as Piscatella pointed out in a follow-up post, Circana's tracking considers disc-less, code-in-box versions to be physical editions. This means Grand Theft Auto 6 will likely overtake the remake in short order, just as it's expected to break records elsewhere.

In Eurogamer's glowing review of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, Christian Donlan argued that Nintendo has done just enough to modernise a timeless classic while maintaining what made the original so special for many players.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a substantial u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the organization and AMERICA.

In a recent development, "On November 12th, our board of directors revealed that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the organization's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones stated during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

Industry observers note that that last bit seems likely to have been stated with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

It has been revealed that "Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the firm navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.".

For now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board confirmed yesterday that they're establishing a "new standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the manufacturer’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is presently serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the organization's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has been updated to support PS Plus Premium cloud streaming directly to the PS5 and PS Portal.

To be crystal clear about this: the game has not been added to the PS Plus Premium catalogue and you will still need to own it.

However, assuming you’ve purchased the game – and millions of you have – then you’ll now be able to stream it directly from Sony’s servers, assuming you’re a PS Plus Premium member.

In a recent development, there are a number of use cases for this, but the most likely is you’re away from your console and still want to play on your PS Portal. Now you won’t need to rely on Remote Play; you can just stream it directly.

This feature wasn’t available at launch, but I’ve been able to test it on my PS5 here in the UK and it’s working well.

There was some reporting prior to release that Microsoft had secured “exclusive” streaming rights to this title, but they were rapidly clarified. This revision now confirms boss Asha Sharma misspoke.

Sources indicate that A few weeks ago, we caught wind of a mysterious countdown taking place on The Pokémon Manufacturer's official social media accounts, marking the hours remaining until 30th November at 2pm UTC. We wondered whether it was all for a surprise eShop drop, a Pokémon Presents or a new Winds & Waves trailer, but it looks like it might all be for something much more disappointing.

As pointed out by Serebii, several of the official Pokémon game social media accounts have begun promoting an upcoming Pokémon music video for a track called 'Evergreen', which will drop on YouTube at, you guessed it, 2pm UTC on 30th November.

Recent findings suggest that it could be that this track is part of something bigger — a Presents segment, or maybe some Gen 10 news — but there's a big part of us now that thinks the countdown was focused on this alone which... we should have tempered our expectations for, to be honest.

*Sigh* We'll pop our tinfoil hats away for now, then...

Original Story: The Pokémon Firm is no stranger to a little over-hyping every now and then, but its latest bit of marketing has us seriously thinking that there is a substantial announcement in the pipeline.

In a recent development, you see, TPC is counting down to... something. As brought to our attention by Serebii's Joe Merrick, the tech giant has been sharing images on social media of its 30th anniversary icons, with a number underneath. Interestingly, these numbers decrease by the number of hours that have passed between each post — 1,025 on 18th October, 843 on 26th, 676 today.

Keeping the countdown going, this means that we'll hit zero on 30th November at 2pm UTC (thanks for doing the maths there, Joe!). The latest post even came with a full message under the logo, roughly translating to "Continue with Pokémon".

Hmm. The big question is, what's this all about? 2pm UTC sure feels like the right time for a big announcement (it's when most eyes, worldwide, will be on it), and we can't imagine that TPC would put this much planning into something inconsequential.

Sources indicate that what is it, then? Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire were rumoured to be coming to NSO last month, could it be that? Is it time we got another look at Winds and Waves, perhaps with a firm release date attached? Is there another full Pokémon Presents around the corner? Only time will tell, but it sure is an exciting prospect.

We'll be keeping an eye on the countdown throughout November and will let you know when any major news comes out of it.

  • Industry observers note that sheets left the show as a full-time cast member in 2019 after suffering a heart attack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Warning: There is discussion of suicide in this story.

Sources indicate that it’s been seven months since Storage Wars star Darrell Sheets died by suicide in his home in Arizona, and it sounds like the other stars of the show, like Brandi Passante, are still, understandably, processing his death. Season 19 of the reality show kicks off on the 2026 television schedule on November 28th, and ahead of its premiere, Passante talked about Sheets’ passing and how it has affected both her personally and the production of the show.

Industry observers note that sheets left the show as a full-time cast member in 2019 after suffering a heart attack. He remained in contact with the rest of the cast, including Passante, and he made occasional guest appearances after retiring. In a discussion with TV Insider, Passante talked about how his death has affected the show, including how the rest of the cast work with each other:.

It definitely changed the dynamic with everybody. We’re all a little softer and kinder to each other since that happened. There was a lot of beef and animosity before between most of us. Some things are not worth fighting.

Sheets’ death, like so many do, really seems to have put things in perspective for the rest of the cast. Their rivalries are what make the show so endlessly watchable, but in the end, they have known each other for almost two decades now, so something like this is bound to change things. Sheets’ manner of death is also a particularly difficult thing to endure, according to Passante:.

According to recent reports, I’ve endured a lot of deaths in that same manner over the years, and that is just a grief that, you know, kind of sticks with you. It’s not like losing somebody to cancer or a heart attack. It’s something that you think maybe you could have helped prevent. It’s one of those difficult deaths that you never can really wrap your head around.

Anyone who has lost a loved one to suicide knows how Passante feels. It can feel completely helpless. For her part, Passante is doing what she can, including checking in on Sheets’ son, Brandon, who was by his father’s side at all the auctions until Darrell left the show. Passante said:.

I talk to [his son] Brandon a lot now. We didn’t really chat much over the years when they left. We would talk every once in a while during holidays or something, but now I just try to keep tabs. He sends me little messages maybe once a week. I just like to check in on him because it’s a hard thing to swallow. I’m sure that he’s missing his dad.

Ultimately, Passante summed it up quite succinctly by saying simply, “It sucks.”.

According to recent reports, there has been a lot of drama on Storage Wars over the years, and while much of it is contrived for the show, behind-the-scenes has been filled with drama, too. Passante has been in the middle of some of it when she divorced her long-time partner in life and in business, Jarrod Schulz, after Season 13 of the show. There has been nothing like the tragedy that befell Sheets, though, and keeping everything in perspective is important.

Sci-fi RPG Exodus continues evoking Mass Effect by revealing female lead and nicknaming her FemJun

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sci-fi role-playing game Exodus continues to play into the Mass Effect comparisons by revealing the female version of its main character Jun, and with studio Archetype referring to her in marketing material as FemJun.
  • If that moniker sounds familiar it's because it is: the female Commander Shepard character in the Mass Effect series was nicknamed FemShep.
  • But there's well publicised BioWare pedigree at Archetype Entertainment, in the studio's co-founders and in the people leading the project.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sci-fi role-playing game Exodus continues to play into the Mass Effect comparisons by revealing the female version of its main character Jun, and with studio Archetype referring to her in marketing material as FemJun.

If that moniker sounds familiar it's because it is: the female Commander Shepard character in the Mass Effect series was nicknamed FemShep. FemShep became an iconic part of BioWare's iconic series, eventually proving that female leads could front games just as successfully as male leads could, and be every bit as popular.

Is the nickname FemJun too blatant? Possibly. But there's well publicised BioWare pedigree at Archetype Entertainment, in the studio's co-founders and in the people leading the project. Key Mass Effect writer Drew Karpyshyn is in charge of writing Exodus, for example, and the similarities to Mass Effect are something the Exodus team has not been shy about in the past. In the wake of Mass Effect 5 being cancelled and BioWare being closed, they become even more alluring.

There are, however, major and important differences between Exodus and Mass Effect, key among them, time dilation. In Exodus, there are special Exodus missions whereby you leave your home planet and fly far away, and in doing so experience time differently to the people back home. Many years will pass for them while only days will pass for you, which provides the game with a way to show you long-term consequences of your actions when you return.

It has been revealed that archetype hasn't shown the female version of Jun before, despite having released many videos of Exodus, perhaps to build anticipation for her reveal. It's a press beat that's also provided Archetype - a studio owned by Dungeons & Dragons manufacturer Wizards of the Coast - with an occasion to reveal the two actors playing Jun in the game.

Female Jun is portrayed by Carina Conti, who played the lead in the recent Mafia game, The Old Country - Isabella Torrisi. She's appeared in HBO's Winning Time and Hulu/Freeform's Good Trouble as well. Male Jun, meanwhile, is portrayed by Stephen Oyoung, who played Mister Negative in Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 1 and 2 games, and Red Hood in Gotham Knights. He also appeared in Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning, The Wrecking Crew, and Twisters. The game also famously stars Matthew McConaughey.

In a recent development, archetype confirmed a Dark Horse hardback art book to go on sale alongside the game next year as well. This arrives a week after the game; Exodus arrives 7th April 2027 on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series S/X, and the art book on 13th April.

Matt played Exodus at Gamescom relatively recently and came away impressed, referring to it as "the best kind of surprise". "I wasn't expecting quite such a bombastic 45 minutes when I first picked up a controller and settled into Exodus, admittedly, but the more I played, the more it made sense," he wrote. "I might not be much of a Mass Effect fan (damn you M35 Mako once more), but Exodus is now firmly on my radar ahead of its arrival next year.".
